item.title: Putin says Russia won't negotiate with Ukraine after bridge strike
item.description:
President Vladimir Putin said Thursday that Russia will not negotiate with Ukraine to agree a limited ceasefire, citing a Ukrainian strike this week on a major bridge connecting Russia and Ukraine's Russian-occupied Crimean Peninsula.
Putin made the remarks to reporters in Russian after meeting with President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China. He said he had discussed the possibility of a ceasefire in certain areas of Ukraine, but would not move forward with negotiations after Ukraine's strike on the Kerch Bridge, according to the Russian state news agencies.
The 12-mile bridge, which Putin ceremonially opened himself in 2018, is hugely symbolic as it links the Russian mainland with Crimea — territory that Russian forces occupied about four years earlier. The missile strike this week wasn't the first time Ukraine had targeted the piece of infrastructure, but it inflicted severe damage. Russia also struck two major bridges in Kyiv the same day.
File photo: A view of Kerch bridge in Crimea in July 2023. Ukraine struck the bridge in mid-November 2026.
Stringer/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images
Putin played down the bridge's strategic importance on Thursday and said he had heard the calls "from all sides" for a naval ceasefire or a suspension of strikes on energy facilities, but he ruled out direct negotiations with Ukraine, citing the attack on the bridge.
"Honestly, I discussed the issue with my colleagues at the Security Council, and I asked them to think about it and go back to the issue, so that we could reach some agreements," Putin said, according to Russian state news agency TASS. "However, we will not make agreements after strikes on the Crimean Bridge. We will respond to these strikes."

item.title: Trump, Xi and Putin sit down for a rare 3-way meeting in China
item.description:
President Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin sat down together in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday in a rare face-to-face encounter for the leaders of three of the world's most powerful countries, but there appeared to be little concrete to show for the meeting in terms of resolving any of the crises facing the world.
The leaders offered a joint statement after their roughly hour-and-a-half-long meeting. Mr. Trump immediately left for his return flight to the U.S. without speaking to journalists on the ground. On the flight home, the president said on social media he will hold a press conference at noon on Friday to discuss the trip.
The presidents discussed Russia's ongoing war in Ukraine, which Mr. Trump has wanted to bring to a negotiated end. But the only significant statement on the conflict came after the meeting from Putin, who ruled out any direct negotiations with Ukraine, citing a major strike earlier this week by Ukrainian forces on a key bridge in Russian-held Crimea.
Putin's senior aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters after the meeting that the atmosphere had been good, and the Kremlin quickly released what it called a joint statement from all three leaders characterizing the talks. The White House later provided the same statement.
Chinese President Xi Jinping, center, President Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin meeting in Shenzhen, China, Nov. 19, 2026.
Mandel NGAN/AFP/Getty

item.title: Iran may be working on biological weapons, Trump says
item.description:
What to know about the Iran war: President Trump told Fox News on Wednesday that there are indications Iran may be working to develop biological or chemical weapons due to damage inflicted to its nuclear program, as tension in the nearly nine-month war appears to rise.Iran claimed Thursday that two more oil tankers had hit sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz, causing fires on board. Iran's daily claims of vessels hitting mines have not been corroborated, but the United Arab Emirates' state oil company confirmed one crew member was missing Wednesday after one of its ships was struck by a projectile.Bahrain and Kuwait said Wednesday that they had intercepted weapons launched by Iran after the U.S. carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya, U.N. top court rules
item.description:
The Hague, Netherlands — In a landmark judgment, the United Nations' top court ruled Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority in a brutal 2017 military operation.
International Court of Justice President Yuji Iwasawa said the court, in a 9-6 decision, found that Myanmar "has committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine state, in violation of its obligations under the Genocide Convention."
The 15-judge panel of the World Court rejected Myanmar's defense that the 2017 campaign was a legitimate operation against insurgents.
Iwasawa said that "the court finds that Myanmar's security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, perpetrated widespread acts of sexual violence, as well as acts of extreme violence against children, and attacked fleeing Rohingya as they sought to flee in large numbers."
Judges led by International Court of Justice (ICJ) President Yuji Iwasawa preside over a hearing at the Peace Palace, the seat of the ICJ, in The Hague, Netherlands,on Nov. 19, 2026, as the court delivers its judgment in the case brought by Gambia accusing Myanmar of genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority.
Mouneb Taim / Anadolu via Getty Images
The decision marks the first time the court has ruled that a state committed genocide.
"This is a great day for the Rohingya, and it is a great day for all oppressed people, everywhere, who have been told that their suffering does not count and that no one is listening," said Yasmin Ullah, a Rohingya rights activist who sat in the court's ornate, wood-paneled Great Hall of Justice for the three-hour reading of the ruling.

item.title: Danish lawmakers OK Greenland security deal with U.S.
item.description:
Copenhagen — Denmark's parliament on Thursday unanimously approved a hard-wrought agreement with Greenland and the United States to strengthen security in the Arctic and North Atlantic.
The vote follows months of pressure by President Trump seeking to control Greenland, a semiautonomous territory of Denmark, a NATO ally.
The trilateral deal among Mr. Trump and Danish and Greenlandic leaders paves the way for more U.S. bases in Greenland and eases tensions over Mr. Trump's repeated calls for the vast, mineral-rich island to become part of the U.S.
The 109-0 vote in the Folketing amounts to a final step: The deal was expected to enter into force once Denmark and Greenland had signed on.
Denmark Foreign Minister Lars Loekke Rasmussen at the first of two readings of an agreement between Denmark, Greenland and the U.S., at Christiansborg Castle, in Copenhagen, Denmark, on Nov. 12, 2026.
Thomas Traasdahl / Ritzau Scanpix via AP
Greenland's parliament approved the deal earlier this month, also with no opposition.
The deal isn't technically a treaty so doesn't need a green light from the U.S. Senate.
The text of the agreement says it will become effective once Denmark and Greenland inform the U.S. "in a diplomatic note" indicating that their parliaments had completed all necessary steps.
The U.S. ambassador to Denmark, Kenneth Howery, welcomed the "strong support" in the Danish parliament for ratification of the deal "paving the way for it to enter into force."
"The agreement is a tremendous accomplishment, one that modernizes our partnership for the security challenges of the future and bolsters the security of the United States, the Kingdom of Denmark, including Greenland, and all of NATO," he wrote on X.

item.title: What to know about Trump's meeting with Xi in China
item.description:
Washington — President Trump is holding a high-stakes meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, against the backdrop of a widening scandal over advanced U.S. chips reaching China and internal divisions within Mr. Trump's Cabinet about how to address it.
The bilateral meeting is taking place in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, known as APEC. Mr. Trump embraced Xi when he arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday.
It's the third time the two world leaders are meeting face to face this year. The last time they met was in September, when Mr. Trump hosted Xi for a three-day summit at the White House. Mr. Trump is hosting Xi again for the G20 Leaders' Summit at Trump National Doral in Miami in December.
The Trump-Xi meeting will be followed by a meeting of Mr. Trump, Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Here's what Mr. Trump and Xi are likely to discuss.
Chinese President Xi Jinping and President Trump attend an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit dinner event in Shenzhen, China, on Nov. 18, 2026.
Qilai Shen / Bloomberg via Getty Images
Jensen Huang, Alice Huang and Nvidia
Mr. Trump told reporters as he left for Asia that he may bring up Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive and suspected Chinese spy who had an affair with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The Justice Department has been investigating Singapore-based Megaspeed for diverting semiconductor chips to China.
The president has cast doubts on assessments that Alice Huang is a Chinese intelligence asset.

item.title: Girlfriend of American killed in Costa Rica arrested
item.description:
American surfer and businessman Kurt Van Dyke was found stabbed and strangled in his Costa Rica home earlier this year. Now, his girlfriend and another man are in custody on suspicion of murder.
Heavily armed Costa Rican police arrested the two in the dark of night last week, some nine months after the 66-year-old was found dead in the town of Puerto Viejo de Talamanca, where he owned a hotel. His 31-year-old girlfriend, whom police have only identified by her last name, Arroyo, survived the attack without any serious injuries, police said initially.
The other person arrested was identified as a 34-year-old man with the last name Gutiérrez. Police allege he and Arroyo "planned a robbery targeting the American with the intent of obtaining the PINs for bank cards" linked to the hotel.
Van Dyke's brother, Peter Van Dyke, told CBS News the revelation that police suspect she was involved in Kurt Van Dyke's death is "shocking."
He said the fact that she was found alive following the attack struck him and his family as "extremely odd," but said he "didn't want to make any speculations."
"We had our suspicions," he said.
Kurt Van Dyke had lived in Costa Rica since the '80s. He comes from a legendary surfing family that pioneered the sport in Santa Cruz, California.
Now that arrests have been made, Peter Van Dyke says the focus is on justice.
"I can't say the word 'happy' because this is not a happy situation," he told CBS News. "We're just satisfied with the outcome so far. I have faith in the Costa Rican law enforcement. It took them nine months, and I totally understand why."
Kurt Van Dyke had three children, and his family said his eldest son plans to be in Costa Rica for the eventual murder trial.

item.title: Florida pastor convicted in plot to kill Haitian president
item.description:
A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted Wednesday of U.S. charges arising from the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse.
Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on all charges, including conspiring to kill Moïse, after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami. He had faced a total of eight charges, the most serious one being conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States.
Sanon, who faces up to life in prison at sentencing, showed little reaction as the verdict was announced in a federal courtroom in Miami.
An attorney for Sanon, Zeljka Bozanic, said in a statement, "We respect the jury's decision, but strongly disagree with the verdict and will file an appeal."
Federal prosecutors said at trial that South Florida was a hub for planning and financing a plot to oust Moïse and install a president of the conspirators' choosing. The prosecutors said Sanon was the conspirators' initial choice for Moïse's replacement. They also said Sanon helped raise money for the conspiracy and arranged travel to Haiti and lodging for himself and others in that country.
Sanon had acknowledged in trial testimony that he was in communication at one point with people trying to replace Moïse, but said the group had moved on to another candidate long before the assassination. He denied any knowledge of plans to kill Moïse.
Sanon was born in Haiti and moved to the U.S. as a teenager. He testified that he worked with churches in Haitian immigrant communities in Florida and the Midwest.
Haiti has not had a president since authorities said that a squad of mostly retired Colombian soldiers killed Moïse and wounded his wife in a nighttime raid at their home on July 7, 2021. The poorest country in the Americas, Haiti has a history of dictatorship, political upheaval and foreign intervention that has long hindered democratic rule.
